analysis.one_liner: Vodafone Idea (Vi) is India's third-largest mobile telecom operator, formed by the 2018 Vodafone-Idea merger and now majority-influenced by the Indian government, which converted unpaid spectrum/AGR dues into a roughly 49% equity stake.
analysis.whats_happening: Vi reported Q2 FY27 (quarter ended 30 Sept 2026) results on 12 November 2026, three days before this note: revenue rose 6.2% YoY to ₹11,884 crore and ARPU improved to ₹198, but the net loss widened to ₹5,975 crore from ₹3,754 crore in the previous quarter as interest costs alone nearly matched the quarter's EBITDA. This comes on the heels of two government interventions - an AGR dues reassessment that cut the liability 27% to ₹64,046 crore (April 2026), and an SBI-led lender consortium's in-principle agreement to extend roughly $3.5 billion for network expansion.
analysis.plain_terms: Vi runs India's third mobile network, competing against Jio and Airtel after years of losing subscribers and racking up dues to the government for spectrum and licence fees. The underlying business is slowly improving - it is charging customers more and shifting them onto 4G/5G, which is lifting revenue and EBITDA. But the company owes so much (net debt of roughly ₹1.96 lakh crore, including deferred government dues) that interest payments alone are swallowing almost all the cash the operations generate - which is why the quarterly loss actually got bigger, not smaller, even as revenue grew. The government has effectively kept Vi alive by converting dues into equity and now owns about half the company, but it has said plainly it will not bail Vi out further, so the next few quarters hinge on banks actually disbursing the funding they have promised.
analysis.quarters: Q2 FY27 (Sept 2026): revenue ₹11,884 crore (+6.2% YoY, +1.7% QoQ), EBITDA ₹4,981 crore (+6.3% YoY, ~42% margin), ARPU ₹198 (+9.7% YoY, up from ₹195 in Q1 FY27) - but net loss widened to ₹5,975 crore from ₹3,754 crore in Q1 FY27, because interest expense (~₹5,351 crore) alone nearly consumed the quarter's entire EBITDA. Q1 FY27 (June 2026) had already shown the first positive net subscriber addition since the 2018 merger (193.1 million vs 192.8 million). These figures are cross-checked across several independent outlets and are mutually consistent; one source's Q2 numbers (₹11,190 crore revenue, ARPU ₹180) look like stale year-ago data mislabeled by calendar year and were set aside. Exact current total/4G subscriber counts could not be independently confirmed - Not verified, check on Screener or the company's investor presentation.
analysis.performance_read: There is no split or demerger in the data to adjust for, so the 89.6% drawdown from the April 2015 peak of ₹120.89 is a genuine, uncompensated loss of capital for anyone who held through the period - not a corporate-action artifact. Over 5 years the stock is up only 24.46% against the Nifty's 38.85% and peer Bharti Airtel's 195.83% - Vi has drastically lagged its chief rival on a multi-year view. The recent 1-year gain of +20.06% (vs Nifty -2.84%) is best read as a relief rally tied to AGR relief and government-support news, not a reversal of the decade-long underperformance; over 3 years the stock is still down 10.53% while Nifty is up 27.8% and Airtel up 127.61%. No dividend has been paid since September 2016.
analysis.valuation_read: The commonly quoted P/E (around -4.4x) and ROE (around 68%) are not meaningful - both come from dividing by a tiny or negative equity base created by years of accumulated losses and the AGR liability sitting on the balance sheet, not from real profitability. P/B is similarly unusable because net worth is negative (-₹44,298 crore as of Sept 2026). So the ~₹1.4 lakh crore market cap isn't really pricing earnings or assets at all - it's pricing two uncertain things: continued government/lender support, and whether ARPU growth can outrun the interest bill. Whether that is 'cheap' or 'expensive' in the normal sense doesn't apply here; it is a bet on survival and turnaround, not a multiple on demonstrated earnings.
analysis.growth_read: Growth is price/mix-led, not volume-led. ARPU rose to ₹198 (+9.7% YoY) mainly from tariff increases and subscribers upgrading to 4G/5G, while the total subscriber base only turned slightly positive for the first time since the merger in Q1 FY27, and 4G population coverage has only recently crossed about 84% - still behind Jio and Airtel. Per the general rule that flat-to-low volume with rising price is less durable than genuine volume growth, this recovery depends on Vi's ability to keep raising prices on a roughly static user base rather than winning share back from rivals.
analysis.health_read: The operating business is genuinely improving - EBITDA grew 6.3% YoY and cash EBITDA margin is up - but the dominant risk here is financial, not operational. Net debt (including deferred spectrum and AGR dues owed to the government) of roughly ₹1.96 lakh crore and negative net worth of ₹44,298 crore mean that almost all operating cash flow is being redirected to debt service: interest expense of about ₹5,351 crore in the latest quarter nearly equalled the entire EBITDA. Little to none of the reported profit improvement is reaching free cash flow available to the company; it still depends on external funding (the SBI-led ~$3.5 billion facility, of which roughly ₹6,400 crore has been disbursed so far) just to fund its 4G/5G network buildout.
analysis.ownership_read: The Government of India is now the largest shareholder at roughly 49%, acquired entirely by converting unpaid spectrum/AGR dues into equity in 2023 and 2025 - the Telecom Minister has stated the government will not raise this stake further or provide additional bailouts. The original promoters (Vodafone Group and the Aditya Birla Group) have been diluted to roughly 25.64% combined; formal pledging is reported at 0%, but promoters have placed a non-disposal undertaking on about 3.28 billion shares (around 18.84% of their holding) as part of funding-related obligations - functionally similar to a pledge in that it restricts free disposal, and worth watching. No marquee independent investor (the kind that signals a conviction bet on a turnaround) shows up on the register; FIIs hold just 5.82% and DIIs 0.33% - institutional ownership outside the government stake is thin.
strengths: ARPU rose to ₹198 in Q2 FY27, up 9.7% YoY and up from ₹195 the prior quarter, showing continued pricing/mix improvement
EBITDA grew 6.3% YoY to ₹4,981 crore with margin near 42%, showing the core operating business is no longer shrinking
AGR dues were reassessed down 27% to ₹64,046 crore in April 2026 (from a provisional ₹87,695 crore), with repayment stretched out toward FY36, materially easing the near-term cash overhang
An SBI-led lender consortium has agreed in principle to roughly $3.5 billion in debt financing, with a first ₹6,400 crore tranche already disbursed for network expansion
watchpoints: Net loss widened to ₹5,975 crore in Q2 FY27 from ₹3,754 crore in Q1 FY27, because interest costs alone nearly consumed the entire quarter's EBITDA
Negative net worth of ₹44,298 crore and net debt of roughly ₹1.96 lakh crore mean the balance sheet remains effectively insolvent without ongoing government/lender support
The government has capped its stake at ~49% and ruled out further bailouts, removing the main backstop that has kept Vi funded so far
4G population coverage has only recently crossed ~84%, still behind Jio and Airtel, and the full ₹25,000-35,000 crore bank facility needed to close that gap is not yet fully tied up
analysis.one_thing: Whether the SBI-led ~$3.5 billion lender facility actually closes and disburses in full, and whether EBITDA growth starts outpacing the roughly ₹5,000+ crore quarterly interest bill - that determines whether the ARPU-led recovery ever reaches the bottom line rather than being absorbed entirely by debt service.
analysis.data_notes: Q2 FY27 revenue (₹11,884 crore), net loss (₹5,975 crore) and ARPU (₹198) were cross-checked across multiple independent outlets (Kotak Securities, Investywise, Business Standard, Beebom, VoiceNData, MarketsMojo) and agreed closely. One source's Q2 figures (₹11,190 crore revenue, ARPU ₹180, 4G/5G subscriber count) appeared inconsistent with this cluster and was set aside as likely stale year-ago data. AGR reassessment amount/timeline and exact current subscriber counts rely on single or lightly-corroborated sources and should be treated as directionally correct but not fully verified - check DoT/company filings. P/E, P/B, ROE and ROCE are sourced from a single aggregator and are distorted by negative net worth, so they are described qualitatively rather than relied on numerically.
